| BP-002 | Supabase's managed `auth.users` is the identity of record and the product's own `users` row is a profile keyed to it, so deleting an account means deleting both. **W1-close catch-up, 2026-09-03** (constitution rule 2.3b, architect's own read; model substituted: sonnet, Opus 529 incident, 2026-09-03). Refuted by this corpus's own approved design, not merely unobserved: (1) `supabase/migrations/00000000000001_baseline.sql` declares `users.id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` — self-generated, never `references auth.users(id)`, and no migration or trigger anywhere in `supabase/migrations/**` links the two tables. (2) BP-032 (`satisfies: [REQ-024]`, approved) is the only provisioning path: `provisionFromPayment` inserts directly into `users` through `dbAdmin()` on a signature-verified Stripe webhook. Its public interface and decisions name no call to Supabase's admin auth API — no `auth.admin.createUser`, no `auth.users` row minted anywhere. (3) BP-061 (`satisfies: [REQ-077]`, approved) is the sign-in mechanism actually specified, and it is a fully custom one: its own `auth_links` table (hashed single-use tokens), its own `issueLink`/`redeemLink`, its own `SessionCookie` — not Supabase's built-in magic-link/GoTrue flow. BP-061 carries its own separate, still-`open` rests-on row recording that the *original* premise was to drive Supabase's magic-link auth through BP-016's mail shell; what it actually specifies bypasses Supabase Auth's token and session mechanism entirely. That row is BP-061's to disposition, not this one's, and is left untouched here. (4) ADR-051 point 6 / BP-063 `purgeAccount` enumerates exactly what a purge removes — 'the account and its address, the site, pages, drafts, measurements, destination credentials ... every copy of the customer's own page content' — with no mention of an `auth.users` row, because none exists to remove. Conclusion: the product's own `users` row is the identity of record outright, not a profile keyed to a Supabase Auth identity — there is no `auth.users` row for it to be 'deleting both' with. This changes no customer promise: REQ-079 criterion 7's erasure guarantee is fully met by BP-063's purge of `users` alone, and BP-002's own body never cited `auth.users` anywhere outside this row, so nothing else in this node depended on the premise. Flagged in this pass's return as a stale premise worth a body note or ADR at the architect's next pass over BP-002 / BP-061, but that edit is out of this catch-up's scope. | undefined | sdlc-factory/docs/blueprints/BP-002.md |

A dedicated test (`domain/parse · a well-formed domain that cannot resolve is accepted`) spies on `dns.lookup`, `dns.resolve` and `fetch` across a real parse and asserts none is called.
